THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MOTOR  VEHICLES ACT, 1988, PRAYING TO SET ASIDE THE JUDGMENT AND  AWARD DATED 01.02.2021 MADE IN MVC NO.2670/2014 PASSED BY  THE VII ADDITIONAL DISTRICT AND SESSIONS JUDGE AND  ADDITIONAL MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL, BELAGAVI,
 SITTING AT CHIKODI, AND ETC.,
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE  COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2023:KHC-D:10655  MFA No. 100926 of 2021  JUDGMENT

The appeal is filed by the owner of the motor-cycle challenging the Judgment and Award dated 01.02.2021 in MVC No.2670/2014 passed by the VII Addl. District and Sessions Judge and Addl.
MACT, Belagavi, sitting at Chikkodi, contending that his motor-cycle is not involved in the accident and his motor-cycle is falsely implicated in the case.

entities.text:
VII Addl. District and Sessions Judge and Addl.
MACT, Belagavi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The factum of the accident, injuries sustained by the claimant/s and liability are not disputed.

3. It is stated in the claim petition that on 05.02.2014 at about 9.25 a.m., the deceased aged about 15 years old was proceeding on his bicycle on Hattarwat- Manganur road to go to school and at that time, the rider of the motor-cycle No.KA-23/Q-6619 riding the same with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, dashed the deceased due to which, the deceased fell down from the bicycle and sustained injuries to the vital organs and succumbed to the injuries.
Therefore, the parents of the NC: 2023:KHC-D:10655 deceased have filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
The Tribunal held that the motor- cycle had caused the accident and granted compensation fixing liability on the appellant who is the owner of motor- cycle.

4. Heard the learned counsel for both sides and perused the records.
5.

Learned counsel for the appellant-owner of the motor-cycle submitted that his motor-cycle was not at all involved in the accident and the motor-cycle has been falsely implicated in the case just to make claim against the appellant-owner.
The appellant being respondent before the Tribunal, has given evidence as RW.1 deposing that his motor-cycle was not involved in the accident.

6. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent/claimant submitted that there are evidences on record that the motor-cycle was involved in the accident and therefore, they have justified the Judgment and Award passed by the Tribunal.

sentences.text: Ex.P1 and Ex.P2 are the F.I.R and complaint given to the Police on 07.02.2014 making allegation against the rider of the motor-cycle No.KA-23/Q-6619 that the deceased was going to school on his bycycle on 05.02.2014 and the rider of the motor-cycle had dashed the deceased resulting death of the deceased.
The police have conducted investigation and filed charge sheet against the rider of motor-cycle.
These are the evidences placed by the claimant apart from the evidence of father of PW.1 proving that the motor-cycle has dashed the deceased and deceased died in the accident.
On the other hand, there is only oral evidence by the appellant-owner of the motor-cycle deposing that motor-cycle is not involved in the accident.
Therefore, upon analysis of the evidence above discussed even though the claimant-PW.1 may not be an eye-witness, but he was informed regarding the accident and death of the deceased in the accident.
Therefore, the evidence of claimant is relevant and admissible as per Section 6 of the Indian Evidence Act.

Furthermore, the evidence of the PW1 is corroborated by NC: 2023:KHC-D:10655 the documentary evidence-Ex.P1, Ex.P2 and FIR,
complaint, charge sheet.
But there is no corroboration to the evidence of RW.1.
The evidence of RW.1 is nothing but self-explanatory in nature without having any corroboration.
Therefore, the claimants have proved that the deceased died in the accident and accordingly, granted compensation.
Therefore, the Judgment and Award passed by the Tribunal needs no interference by this Court.
Appeal is liable to be dismissed.

8. Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) Appeal is dismissed.
ii) The Judgment and Award dated 01.02.2021 in MVC No.2670/2014 passed by the VII Addl. District and Sessions Judge and Addl. MACT, Belagavi, sitting at Chikkodi,
is hereby confirmed.
iii) No order as to costs.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:10655 iv) Registry to transmit the T.C.R to the Tribunal along with a copy of this Judgment forthwith.
